objections: Every query was run against OpenAlex 'works' full-text search — a corpus of peer-reviewed academic literature. Commercial streaming records are reported by Spotify's own newsroom and trade press (Billboard, Variety, Chartmetric blogs), which OpenAlex does not index. All four zero-result searches are therefore guaranteed artifacts of source selection, not evidence about the world; treating them even as weak (0.05) signal against the record is unfounded.

The one retrieved item is a BYU music-education abstract about school students' perceptions of popular songs — matched only because OpenAlex fuzzy-matched the word string. It shares no entity with the question beyond generic music vocabulary, yet it occupies 1 of 2 nonzero evidence slots, structurally contaminating any downstream scoring with pure noise.

The queries embed the conclusion's own vocabulary ('record', 'exceed previous record holder') into fulltext boolean filters, guaranteeing near-zero recall for any article phrased differently ('biggest debut', 'single-week high'). Failure-by-construction of the search is then read as absence of support — classic tooling-induced selection, not evidence about whether the record was broken.

Even absent stream counts, publicly known priors as of April 2024 independently explain an expected 'yes': TTPD broke Spotify's single-day album record on day one and had the largest presales/first-day streams ever reported, making the prior record holder's total irrelevant to the outcome. Any pipeline output near 0.00-0.05 confidence reflects retrieval failure, not a genuine case that the conclusion is wrong.
refusal_reason: confidence 0.0 below DB floor 0.3 after adversary penalties
text: Will 'The Tortured Poets Department' become Spotify's most-streamed album in a single week upon release (May 2024)?
